main_body: A tall narrow tile-strip of wooden fence/farm posts: repeated light-tan capped blocks on the left column and thin dark vertical rails on the right, with grey metal bits at a few rows. Reads as a repeating strip of small fence segments.
top_band: Per segment, a light tan cap (L=181) 1 row at x=2 (2 rows at x=7) over a mid-brown face (L=131), then dark brown; no multi-row lighter top surface. Column x=5 is a single dark run (L=30) with no top band.
evidence: The tan cap is only 1-2 px, which is a rim and not a top surface. Segments repeat every 6 or 16 rows with a dark gap between them. The drawing is a tiled strip of posts, not a frame with horizontal beams and a base showing top faces. The right-hand rails are plain vertical dark bars. The result is a front elevation with a thin rim, and it does not match the frame kind.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 6 distinct colours and a median of 6 per tile, against 38-40 distinct and 17-20 per tile in the references. Its ramps are shallow: tan, mid-brown and dark brown, with a near-black column. The dark edge pixels are tinted brown (0% neutral), so the outline is material-toned, but the surfaces carry no grain, dots or per-element shading. It looks thinner and flatter than the roofed well and cheese stall.
